# Session, shortcuts and help

## tritonctl configure

Write settings, and log in only when credentials are given.

With only settings flags (--endpoint, --sso-issuer, --project) it writes them without prompting and without touching a stored session. With --username or --password-stdin (or with no flags at all) it runs the password login as before.

Usage: `tritonctl configure [OPTIONS]`

- `--endpoint <ENDPOINT>`: Endpoint to store (and, for a password login, to authenticate against)
- `--sso-issuer <URL>`: Sign-in service for `login --sso`, stored for later logins: `https://<sign-in host>/realms/<realm>`, where the realm is your silo (e.g. `https://id.example.com/realms/9cf1f427-...`). Your administrator has it
- `--username <USERNAME>`: Username (prompted for on a password login)
- `--password-stdin`: Read the password from stdin instead of prompting
- `--sso`: Sign in through your identity provider (browser) once the settings are written, instead of with a password

## tritonctl login

Re-authenticate against the configured endpoint

Usage: `tritonctl login [OPTIONS]`

- `--endpoint <ENDPOINT>`
- `--username <USERNAME>`
- `--password-stdin`
- `--sso`: Sign in through your identity provider (device flow) instead of a password
- `--issuer <URL>`: Sign-in service for --sso, `https://<sign-in host>/realms/ <realm>` (the realm is your silo). Defaults to TRITONCTL_SSO_ISSUER, then the stored one

## tritonctl logout

Remove stored credentials

Usage: `tritonctl logout [OPTIONS]`

## tritonctl whoami

Show the current identity and effective scope

Usage: `tritonctl whoami [OPTIONS]`

## tritonctl env

Print shell exports for the current session

Usage: `tritonctl env [OPTIONS]`

## tritonctl api

One request to the control plane, with your session

Usage: `tritonctl api [OPTIONS] <METHOD> <PATH>`

- `<METHOD>`: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE
- `<PATH>`: The path, starting with `/`, query string included
- `-d, --data <DATA>`: The request body: JSON text, or `@FILE`, or `@-` for stdin
- `--header <NAME: VALUE>`: A request header, as `Name: value`. Repeatable. (No `-H`: that is the global no-headers flag.)
- `-i, --include`: Print the status line and response headers on stderr
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails

## tritonctl port-forward

Forward a local port to a port on an instance

Usage: `tritonctl port-forward [OPTIONS] <PORTS> <TARGET>`

- `<PORTS>`: LOCAL or LOCAL:REMOTE ports
- `<TARGET>`: Instance name or uuid
- `--subnet <SUBNET>`: Which of the instance's networks to reach it on
- `--bind <BIND>`: Address to listen on (default: 127.0.0.1)

## tritonctl ssh-config

Print an ssh_config block that reaches instances as NAME.triton

Usage: `tritonctl ssh-config [OPTIONS]`

## tritonctl activity

What happened in your tenant, newest first

Usage: `tritonctl activity [OPTIONS]`

- `--in-project <PROJECT>`: Only events in this project (name, uuid, or prefix). Defaults to the one you work in; `--all` for the whole tenant
- `--all`: Every project of the tenant
- `--last <LAST>`: How many events, newest first (default: 50)

## tritonctl completion

Print a shell completion script.

Install it once, then start a new shell:

  tritonctl completion bash > /usr/local/etc/bash_completion.d/tritonctl
  tritonctl completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_tritonctl"
  tritonctl completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/tritonctl.fish

Usage: `tritonctl completion [OPTIONS] <SHELL>`

- `<SHELL>` (one of: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh)

## tritonctl ls

A shortcut for `tritonctl instance list`

Usage: `tritonctl ls [OPTIONS]`

- `--image <IMAGE>`: Only instances from this image (name, name@version, uuid, or prefix)
- `--state <STATE>`: Only instances in this lifecycle state (one of: pending, provisioning, running, stopping, stopped, deleting, failed)

## tritonctl create

A shortcut for `tritonctl instance create`

Usage: `tritonctl create [OPTIONS] --name <NAME> --image <IMAGE> --subnet <SUBNET>`

- `--name <NAME>` (required)
- `--description <DESCRIPTION>`
- `--image <IMAGE>`: Image to boot (name, name@version, uuid, or prefix) (required)
- `--subnet <SUBNET>`: Subnet for the primary NIC (name, uuid, or prefix) (required)
- `--ssh-key <KEY>`: SSH key to install (name, fingerprint, uuid, or prefix). Repeatable
- `--package <PACKAGE>`: Size it from a package (name, name@version, uuid, or prefix) instead of --cpu and --memory. The package's default disks apply unless a --disk names its own
- `--cpu <CPU>`: Virtual CPUs. Needed without --package
- `--memory <SIZE>`: Memory: `4G`, `512M`, or bytes. Needed without --package
- `--disk <SPEC>`: A disk. Repeatable: `boot,type=replicated[,replicas=N][,tier=T]` puts the boot disk on replicated storage; `size=100G,type=replicated[,replicas=N][,tier=T]` adds a data disk; a bare `50G` sizes the boot disk
- `--tag <KEY=VALUE>`: A tag, as key=value. Repeatable
- `--data-disk <SIZE[,replicas=N][,tier=T]>`: A data disk replicated to other compute nodes: `100G`, with optional `,replicas=2` (3 by default) and `,tier=standard` (`performance` by default). The same as `--disk size=SIZE,type=replicated,...`. Repeatable
- `--user-data <FILE>`: cloud-init user data: a file path, or `-` for stdin
- `--wait`: Wait until the change has taken effect, then print the instance. Progress goes to stderr; gives up after 15 minutes

## tritonctl delete

A shortcut for `tritonctl instance delete`

Alias: rm

Usage: `tritonctl delete [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Instance name, uuid, or prefix
- `--force`: Delete an instance that is not stopped or failed. The server still decides
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails
- `--wait`: Wait until the change has taken effect, then print the instance. Progress goes to stderr; gives up after 15 minutes

## tritonctl ssh

SSH to an instance through the platform relay.

Execs OpenSSH with a ProxyCommand; every ssh option after `--` is passed through.

Usage: `tritonctl ssh [OPTIONS] <TARGET> [-- <ARGS>...]`

- `<TARGET>`: Instance name or UUID. `user@name` sets the login; the default login is root
- `--login <LOGIN>`: Login name on the instance. Overrides a `user@` prefix. No `-l`: that is the global long-output flag here
- `<ARGS>...`: Arguments passed to ssh verbatim

## tritonctl tunnel

Copy stdin and stdout to a port on an instance.

This is what `ssh` runs as its ProxyCommand. Nothing is printed on stdout, which carries the connection.

Usage: `tritonctl tunnel [OPTIONS] <TARGET>`

- `<TARGET>`: Instance name or UUID
- `--port <PORT>`: Destination TCP port (default: 22)
- `--subnet <SUBNET>`: Which of the instance's networks to reach it on (name, uuid, or prefix)
